title: Fog on the Thames
teaser: Rain, red buses, a frightened solicitor, and a murder on the Embankment.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: London. Rain that doesn't fall so much as hang in the air and wait for you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Oliver Ashworth's office at Lincoln's Inn smells of old paper and older secrets.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: Someone was here last night. They took nothing. Which means they were looking for something they didn't find.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: The first half of the will. And a key. The Chief said only his blood could open his box in Geneva.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: I never understood what he meant. Perhaps one of you does.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: And one more thing. Near the end, the Chief told me Elise Moreau was never working alone. 'Every wolf has a shepherd,' he said. I thought he was being poetic.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen's hand closes around the coral bracelet in her pocket.

scenes.prompt: Oliver looks like a man who hasn't slept in a week.

choices.text: "Come with us to Geneva, Oliver. You're not safe here."

response.speaker: oliver
response.text: That's... very kind. I have one thing to collect first. Meet me on the Embankment at nine.

choices.text: "How do we know you're not part of this?"

response.speaker: oliver
response.text: You don't. That's rather the point of trust.

response.speaker: oliver
response.text: The Embankment, nine o'clock. There's something you need to see.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nine o'clock. Fog on the Embankment, and lamps like drowned moons.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Oliver is late. Then he isn't late. He's lying on the stone steps down to the river.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: ...Moreau... and the shepherd... the shepherd...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His hand opens. In his palm is a small brass key.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Footsteps, running. A shadow in a long coat is disappearing toward Waterloo Bridge.

response.speaker: oliver
response.text: Tell the girl... her father... was so proud...

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Oliver Ashworth, solicitor, sixty-one years old, dies on the steps of the Thames as the fog closes over him.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Down the Embankment, across the bridge, and into a black car with Swiss diplomatic plates.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: When the chase is over, so is Oliver.

choices.text: Call the police. Do this properly.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: The Met arrive in eleven minutes. Oliver Ashworth has been dead for ten.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A pub off the Strand, near closing. Nobody is drinking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kolade keeps checking his phone. Every time it buzzes, he turns it face down.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: They killed him for a key. For a KEY.

lines.speaker: hadiza
lines.text: They killed him because he knew where the money went. And now so do we.

scenes.prompt: London has already taken one life.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: My mother.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Nobody believes him. Nobody can prove otherwise, either.

choices.text: "We finish this. For the Chief, and for Oliver."

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: For Oliver.

response.speaker: tari
response.text: For the Chief.

choices.text: Trust no one at this table.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: In this game, the cautious ones live longest.

choices.text: Read Oliver's diary aloud: "My shame: I knew about Geneva for two years and said nothing."

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: He knew. And he died trying to make it right.

response.speaker: tari
response.text: Then we finish what he started.

choices.text: Lay the blackened spoon on the table. "E.M. Elise Moreau. She killed the Chief."

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Nobody touches it. Everybody stares at it.

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: Then Geneva is not a bank visit. It is a hunt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A pub off the Strand, near closing. Kolade's phone buzzes. Geneva.

lines.speaker: phone
lines.text: Unfortunate about the solicitor. Bring me the key, Monsieur Balogun. Then the crown is yours.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: They killed him for a key. For a KEY.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the table, Nabyen is crying without making a sound.

scenes.prompt: Elise wants the key. The others are watching Kolade.

choices.text: Tell them everything about Elise's offer.

response.speaker: tari
response.text: You WHAT?

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: ...Then she trusts him. That's useful. Very useful.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: Thank you for telling us. Don't ever lie to me again.

choices.text: Say nothing. Text Elise one word: 'Soon.'

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Sent. Delivered. Read.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the parapet, under a lamp, someone has left a white lily. Nobody touches it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Westminster Bridge, two in the morning. Nabyen has been crying, and is pretending she hasn't.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Everyone who gets close to this ends up dead.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Maybe you should go home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Westminster Bridge, two in the morning. Tari found her, because Tari always finds her.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: I'm not going home. Not without you.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: The roses. Every birthday since you were twelve. The notes. W.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: The Chief asked me to watch over you. I never told him I had fallen in love with you.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: ...You. It was always you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Westminster Bridge, two in the morning. Kolade found her, with two cups of terrible coffee.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Lagos can wait. You can't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Westminster Bridge, two in the morning. She's alone, and that's how she wanted it.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Her mouth tastes of rain and London and something like home. The fog swallows the bridge, the river, the whole city, until there is nobody left in London but the two of you.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: ...Okay. So that happened.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: Good. I'd hate to have to come and find you.

choices.text: Walk her back to the hotel without a word.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Some silences say more than speeches. This is one of them.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: He kisses her like a man who has waited twenty years and is done waiting. Big Ben strikes again. Neither of them hears it.

response.speaker: tari
response.text: Twenty years I've wanted to do that.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: The coffee goes into the Thames. His hand at the small of her back, careful, as if she might vanish. For once, Kolade Balogun isn't performing for anyone.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: For once in my life, I have nothing clever to say.

response.speaker: kaneng
response.text: My daughter. Come home in one piece. That is all I'm asking.

outcomes.title: Thirty Pieces of Silver
outcomes.text: Kolade chose Elise. Nobody knows yet. Everybody will.

outcomes.title: The Confession
outcomes.text: Kolade told the truth when lying would have been easier. That's rarer than gold.

outcomes.title: A Kiss in the Fog
outcomes.text: A man died tonight, and something else began. London is like that.

outcomes.title: Death on the Embankment
outcomes.text: Oliver Ashworth died for a brass key. The killers are already in Geneva.

reflections.text: Oliver's last words were for Nabyen.
Swiss diplomatic plates. Whoever this is, they're protected.

s_shame.title: Oliver's diary
s_shame.text: SHAME. From Oliver's diary, found in his coat: 'My shame: I knew about Geneva for two years and said nothing.'

m_london.title: Rain at Lincoln's Inn
m_london.text: Red buses, old paper, and a frightened man with a key.

m_bridge.title: Westminster, 2 a.m.
m_bridge.text: Fog, lamplight, and Big Ben striking two.

k_voice_oliver.title: Oliver's last voicemail
k_voice_oliver.text: If you're hearing this, I didn't make it to the Embankment. The key opens the vault. The blood opens the truth. And look after the girl. Please.

epigraph.text: London keeps its secrets the way the Thames keeps its dead.
